title: Fee schedule definition, versioning and cost basis
status_rationale: Specified in Unbound requirements (cited) but not implemented; no production deployment, operating evidence or independent review exists (architecture/ECHELON-CURRENT-STATE-BRIEF.md).
target_answer: Every fee schedule is an approved, effective-dated version that declares its FeeBase contract: measurement basis (end-of-day market value by default; average daily, period-end or quarter-average options), inclusions and exclusions, valuation version, tier method, day count, accrual and settlement cadence, minimums, waivers, payer source, recipient type, service identity and treatment of reserved-but-uncommunicated grants. Accrued unpaid fees and fees already embedded in pool or manager NAV are excluded from any base. A schedule that sets a minimum annual fee or minimum balance must reference a current cost basis record (no older than 13 months) and either stay within a configured ratio to fully allocated cost or record a disclosed non-cost rationale. Schedules are scoped per sponsor, partner and program and never leak across partners.

title: Fee calculation accuracy, transparency and reconciliation
status_rationale: Specified in Unbound requirements (cited) but not implemented; no production deployment, operating evidence or independent review exists (architecture/ECHELON-CURRENT-STATE-BRIEF.md).
target_answer: Fee administration runs as an idempotent run per (fund, schedule, period, segment set) through Accrued, Assessed, Posted and optionally Waived or Reversed; replaying a run posts nothing new, and corrections are compensating entries. Every accrual stores its computed base and inputs and is deterministically recomputable, so any donor or auditor can see base, rate, days and result. Only the fee engine emits authoritative fee events; informational events cannot change fee state. Fees are never charged twice at pool and fund level. Advisor or manager fee debits visible in custodian feeds are recorded as distinct transactions and reconciled; where feeds do not expose them they are raised as reconciliation exceptions. Fees embedded in manager NAV are disclosed as such.

challenge.customer_intent: Fees charged are exactly what the schedule says.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Systematic overcharging, donor complaints, refunds and reputational harm.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Periodic sample recalculation of a few accounts by staff or auditors detects only gross errors.
challenge.legally_required: No statute prescribes fee recalculation for DAF sponsors.
challenge.contractually_required: Sponsors and auditors expect fee accuracy testing.
challenge.historical_convention: Quarterly spot checks and annual audit sampling.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Arithmetic and double-posting errors largely eliminated by deterministic, idempotent runs with decimal types; schedule configuration errors are not.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Every accrual is recomputed independently and compared before posting.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Stored base and inputs for every accrual enable 100 percent recomputation.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Full-population recomputation each run instead of sampling.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes; an auditor can re-run the recomputation.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: The recomputation shares the same flawed schedule configuration, so it confirms consistent but wrong fees.
challenge.alternative_cost: Compute cost negligible; build cost moderate.
challenge.alternative_risks: False confidence when configuration itself is wrong.
opposing_arguments: Independent recomputation by the same system is not independent of configuration errors; configuration review is still needed.

title: Fee change control, waivers and donor notice
status_rationale: Specified in Unbound requirements (cited) but not implemented; no production deployment, operating evidence or independent review exists (architecture/ECHELON-CURRENT-STATE-BRIEF.md).
target_answer: Fee schedules change only by approving a new effective-dated version through the sponsor's configuration governance, which detects conflicts with platform hard controls, encoded law and pack baselines before approval; changes are by supersession, never in-place edits, and never retroactive. Waivers are approved schedule exceptions with reason and expiry. AI may draft a proposed change but cannot approve it. Donor-facing quotes are shown for charged operations and any amount above the donor's accepted maximum requires consent or is absorbed by the sponsor. A minimum advance-notice period for fee increases is a sponsor policy that Unbound should enforce as a release gate; no such requirement exists yet.

title: Grant priority over fees and fee shortfall handling
status_rationale: Specified in Unbound requirements (cited) but not implemented; no production deployment, operating evidence or independent review exists (architecture/ECHELON-CURRENT-STATE-BRIEF.md).
target_answer: Recognized grants payable and, by default, reserved grants rank ahead of fees. A fee shortfall becomes a fund-level memo claim against future capacity, not an entity-level asset; it may be waived by an authorized approver with a reason and is written off on fund closure. Fee schedules declare their treatment of reserved-but-uncommunicated grants. Fund closure posts final fees as a defined state before residual disposition, with no closing-period minimum or proration unless the schedule version states it. During a dispute freeze, fees accrue and are collected while grants are held; waiver is a separate decision.

title: Donor-covered, pass-through and processing fees
status_rationale: Specified in Unbound requirements (cited) but not implemented; no production deployment, operating evidence or independent review exists (architecture/ECHELON-CURRENT-STATE-BRIEF.md).
target_answer: When fee coverage is voluntary and the sponsor is merchant of record, the acknowledgment amount is the gross amount charged, the fund is credited gross, and the processing fee posts as an expense (to the fund only if the schedule discloses pass-through). Amounts paid to a non-charity (platform or mandatory convenience fees) are excluded from the acknowledgment and shown separately. Donor-paid service fees are receipted as service fees with no deductibility statement. Bank return and intermediary fees are borne by the sponsor by default, domestic wires are sent without deductions and international wires default to OUR; any pass-through is disclosed. Required accessibility accommodations carry no fee. Card contributions, and therefore donor-covered card fees, are deferred beyond release 1.

title: Revenue sharing, advisor compensation and conflict disclosure
status_rationale: Specified in Unbound requirements (cited) but not implemented; no production deployment, operating evidence or independent review exists (architecture/ECHELON-CURRENT-STATE-BRIEF.md).
target_answer: Referral attribution is recorded as an immutable informational fact; Unbound computes, accrues or exports no referral compensation unless a counsel-approved rule for that arrangement and jurisdiction exists. Decided rule: referral compensation is never paid from fund assets; flat fair-market-value fees from sponsor operating funds are permitted only under written agreement, to persons who are not advisors or related parties of the referred fund, in states where paid-solicitor rules are satisfied, and never per grant or per dollar granted. No compensation or other payment is made from a fund to a donor, donor-advisor (including an advisor the donor designated with investment privileges), family member or 35 percent controlled entity; advisor or manager compensation from DAF assets is held until the advisor relationship is classified by counsel. Sponsor-engaged managers may be paid only under sponsor contracts with uniform program-wide fees. Echelon itself takes no compensation varying with assets, trades or liquidations. Disclosure of Echelon's own relationships with sponsors (including any board overlap) is an organizational matter not yet established.

challenge.customer_intent: Fees and incentives do not compromise donor interests or create excess benefit.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Excise taxes under sections 4958 or 4967, reputational damage, conflicted advice.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Disclosure documents and annual conflict certifications; weak at preventing payments.
challenge.legally_required: Section 4958 treats compensation from a DAF to a donor or donor-advisor as an excess benefit; paid-solicitor registration applies in many states.
challenge.contractually_required: Sponsors increasingly require conflict disclosure from vendors.
challenge.historical_convention: Disclosure of revenue sharing in program descriptions; advisor fees often paid from DAF assets.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Partly: payments to related parties from fund assets are blocked by a nonwaivable related-party hold; referral compensation cannot be computed from fund data without an approved rule.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Accrual hold when advisor classification is missing.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Related-party registry checks logged per payment.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Structural prohibition plus disclosure, rather than disclosure alone.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Likely among sponsors; possibly unwelcome to advisor channels whose economics depend on asset-based fees.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Related-party registry incomplete; advisor relationships not disclosed by donors.
challenge.alternative_cost: Moderate build; may reduce channel revenue.
challenge.alternative_risks: Commercial disadvantage versus platforms that pay advisors from DAF assets.
supporting_arguments: Prevents the highest-severity tax outcome rather than disclosing it.
Removes per-dollar incentives that create conflicts.
opposing_arguments: Advisor-managed DAF programs commonly pay asset-based advisory fees from fund assets; a strict hold may make Unbound unattractive to that channel.
Registry completeness depends on donor self-disclosure.
